queries.hook: A fire lit by the feeling of being alive and building something of your own, and the resolve to keep it burning when the money is gone.
queries.diagnose: Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the prize or looks sideways at others; it holds when the work itself is the reward.
queries.steady: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.
queries.story: A young warrior who set out to win what was theirs to win, faced the first setback, and kept their resolve through it.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna reminds Arjuna of his duty as a warrior and what retreat would cost him.
verse.sanskrit: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ । ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
verse.line: Hold pleasure and pain, gain and loss, win and defeat as equal. Then step in and act.
verse.translation: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike, then engage in the fight. Done this way, you will incur no wrong.
verse.why: Decide from steadiness, not from fear of winning or losing.

prasang.title: Why a warrior must fight: duty
prasang.summary: Krishna appeals to Arjuna's sense of duty and honour, then tells him to treat victory and defeat alike before he acts.
prasang.lesson: Decide from steadiness, not from fear of winning or losing.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, telling him that retreating from the fight will only bring disgrace and endless shame. He says to treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same thing. Then step in and do what must be done. Done this way, you will not incur any wrong. The idea is to act from a steady place, not from the fear of winning or losing.
verse.for_you: You have left the safety of a job and the money is not here yet. That is exactly what this asks of you. Treat the thrill of starting out and the stress of the empty account as the same. Step in and build your brand anyway, because the work is yours to do.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verse.sanskrit: पुरुषार्थात्फलप्राप्तिर्देशकालवशादिह । प्राप्ता चिरेण शीघ्रं वा यासौ दैवमिति स्मृता ॥
verse.line: Effort brings results, sooner or later, depending on time and place. That timing is what we call fate.
verse.translation: Results come from effort, sooner or later, depending on place and time. That arrival of the fruit, early or late, is what people call fate.
verse.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha is speaking to Rama. Rama has just learned that his father was killed by his own uncle, and he is sitting in despair. Vasishtha tells him that the future is not a locked door. He says that what people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, arriving early or late. He tells Rama that his own present effort can overcome any past. The effort you put in today is what will shape tomorrow, and you could not waste your energy grieving what was never in your hands.
verse.for_you: You quit your job last week and the money has not come yet. This verse says that the timing of your results is not your fault. Your effort is the only thing that matters, so let it be enough for today.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari spoke this to the reader, sitting at a time when the world feels like it is throwing everything at them. The verse says that let the wise praise or blame. Let money come or go. Let death come today or ages from now. The steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right. The point is that setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.
verse.for_you: The morning comes and the work feels heavy. The praise from strangers has not arrived. Let the money come or go. You do not need to step off the path you chose. Just keep going.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
verse.line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
verse.translation: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: In the forest, Draupadi speaks to Yudhishthira. She is tired of watching the good suffer while waiting for fate to fix things. She says that simply waiting for a reward is a losing game. Every action you take can end in two ways, success or not. If you do nothing, you are certain to fail. She tells him to stop worrying about results and just do what is right, while working as if the whole future depends on his own hands.
verse.for_you: You have quit your job to build your brand. The money has not arrived yet, but the feeling of being alive is still strong. Let that feeling carry you through the tasks that do not excite you today.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verse.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, seeing him hesitate. He tells him that his duty is to act, to fight, without being attached to whether he wins or loses. The right to act belongs to him alone. The outcome is not in his hands. Do the work with full attention, but let go of the need to control the result.
verse.for_you: The work is building your brand. The result is still out of reach. Do the work today as if the result does not exist, and let the work itself be the reward.

verse.line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
verse.translation: One who begins only after deciding, does not stop halfway through the work, does not waste time and keeps himself in hand, is called wise.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

verse.meaning: Vidura speaks to King Dhritarashtra, who lies awake in the dark before the peace talks. He tells the king that a wise person decides calmly, acts steadily, and does not stop halfway. They do not waste time or lose their grip on themselves. The point is that real happiness comes from clear action, not from waiting for the right moment.
verse.for_you: You decided to leave the job and you began. Now the money has not come and the morning alarm feels heavy. Do not let that heaviness make you stop. Decide again, this morning, that the work is yours, and begin the small task in front of you without pausing halfway.

story.title: Hanuman's leap
story.story_hook: Halfway across the ocean, a golden mountain rose out of the water and offered him a place to rest.
story.summary: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.
story.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

anchor.sanskrit: यस्य त्वेतानि चत्वारि वानरेन्द्र यथा तव। धृतिर्दृष्टिर्मतिर्दाक्ष्य स कर्मसु न सीदति ॥

story.for_you: Hanuman crossed the ocean by knowing when to be large and when to be small. They did not stop to rest, and they did not let the size of the water make them small either. Your own build will ask you to shrink back into the old job sometimes.

script: You left your job last week. You are building your own brand now. The money is not here yet. But you feel alive. You do not want that feeling to leave.

On a battlefield, Krishna speaks to Arjuna. Arjuna wants to drop his weapons and walk away. Krishna reminds him that running from the fight will bring shame and disgrace. Krishna tells him to look at pleasure and pain as the same. He tells him to look at gain and loss as the same. He tells him to look at victory and defeat as the same. And then Krishna says: step in and act. Krishna said:
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ, ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि.
In plain words: Hold pleasure and pain, gain and loss, win and defeat as equal. Then step in and act.

This is a hard thing to do. It is easier said than done, because every morning you will feel the thrill of starting something new. You will also feel the stress of the empty account. The verse asks you to hold both of those feelings as equal. It asks you to act from a steady place. It asks you to decide from steadiness, not from the fear of winning or losing.

Tomorrow morning, when you open your laptop to work on your brand, notice the excitement in your chest. Notice the worry about money right next to it. Let them both be there. Do not let the worry stop the work. Step in and build anyway.
What is yours to build is waiting.

depth.points: Decide from steadiness, not from fear of winning or losing. The cost of retreat is measured in regret, not in rupees. Your duty is to the work itself.

depth.question: What is the work itself, when the money is not there?
